synth.title: i18n text-expansion + multi-script typography grounding
synth.principle_summary: Text-expansion planning must be keyed to source-string CHARACTER LENGTH, not to a per-language flat percentage: the IBM/W3C curve runs from 100-200% increase under 10 characters down to 30% over 70 characters, so short UI strings (chips, tabs, CTA labels, exactly Solen's fixed-width surfaces) are the worst-case band, not the best case a flat "German +30%" implies. German is also not a safe worst-case proxy for Solen's other Latin locales: the one available per-language datapoint ranks Italian (3.0x) above German (2.8x) above French (2.6x). When real shipped products hit this problem they resolve it three ways, in order of preference: shorten the copy at translation time (Fresha, Treatwell), let the container size to content instead of clamping (Booksy), or wrap to a second line (Discord, Doctolib). None resolve it with shrink-to-fit font scaling or mid-word ellipsis-truncation on a primary CTA or nav chip, which is the concrete anti-pattern D9's overflow audit should test for. Separately, the specific "German expands ~30%" number circulating in 2026 trend content traces to an SEO content-farm citation that does not even contain the figure, confirming it as folklore rather than an independently-corroborated second source.
synth.proposed_addition:
RATIONALE.md section 9 (Domain 9: i18n typography), replacing the line-206 bucket sentence and adding a new resolution-strategy mechanic, same CONV/T2 framing, no LOCKFILE literal touched:

DECISION: State the IBM/W3C character-bucket expansion curve in ONE consistent unit (percentage increase over the English source length); stop treating German as the presumptive worst-case Solen locale; and name the three real-world resolution strategies for a fixed-width slot that overflows, ranked by preference, so D9 has a concrete pass/fail vocabulary instead of a single number.

FORCES: fixed-width UI slots (chips, tabs, badge pills, button labels) must be sized against the longest rendered locale, not the EN draft. The correct slack number depends on the source string's character length, not on which of the four locales it renders in. Mixing "percent of original" and "percent increase" conventions in the same table produces a silently wrong slack budget for mid-length strings. And when a slot still overflows after correct sizing, the component needs a named fallback strategy, not an ad hoc clamp.

OPTIMIZES FOR: a single readable planning table an implementer can apply without re-deriving units; a named, shippable-precedent-backed decision tree for overflow (shorten, then widen-to-content, then wrap) instead of defaulting to truncation; permanently closing SOURCE.md:1075's already-flagged folklore gap with a real source and a debunked myth-chain, so nobody re-imports "German +30%" from a future trend-roundup search.

SACRIFICES: precision. The underlying IBM table is pooled across European languages (not German-specific, not per-locale) and its 51-70 bucket does not monotonically decrease versus the 31-50 bucket, an artifact this entry notes rather than smooths over. The per-language ranking (Italian over German) rests on one word pair (Flickr's "views"), so it is directional test-string guidance, not a settled per-language law. The competitor resolution-strategy evidence is CONV (live-fetched real screens, not a controlled study) and Doctolib's observation is partial (footer-only, no fetchable booking-flow CTA text).

BOUNDARY: no line-height rule follows for Solen's own locale set. The W3C source's vertical-space guidance (Thai roughly 150% of Latin line height, extra headroom for CJK/Arabic/Devanagari/Tibetan) applies to non-Latin scripts only; de/en/fr/it are all Latin, so domain 9's existing boundary line ("RTL and CJK: out of scope by locale set") already correctly excludes this. Separately, "variable font width axis for language compression" is explicitly NOT a documented multilingual-expansion technique in current design-trend or technical sources (checked directly, absent from both the typography-trend roundups and the localization literature): do not let a future pass bridge "variable fonts are a 2026 trend" into "therefore compress German with a width axis" without new evidence. This finding narrows, it does not expand, the multi-script surface.

MECHANIC (T2, IBM "Guidelines to design global solutions" via W3C Internationalization "Text size in translation"): planning buckets for percentage increase over the English source string, by source character count: under 10 chars, 100-200% (the translation can run 2-3x the source length); 11-20 chars, 80-100%; 21-30 chars, 60-80%; 31-50 chars, 40-60%; 51-70 chars, 51-70% (source-table anomaly, use the wider 40-70% band for planning); over 70 chars, 30%. Chips, tabs, and buttons sit in the under-20-char band, the largest-expansion band, which is why the LOCKFILE <=3-word CTA lock and the truncation-with-affordance rule carry real weight.

MECHANIC (T2, same source, single-word example, pooled-language caveat applies): do not treat German as the automatic worst-case Solen locale for short strings. The one available per-language ratio (Flickr's "views" label, English = 1.0x) ranks Italian 3.0x above German 2.8x above Portuguese and French at 2.6x each. Any Solen fixed-width slot test-string set should include an Italian and a French candidate alongside the German one, not German alone.

MECHANIC (CONV, live competitor fetches 2026-07-22): three observed resolution strategies for a fixed-width slot that overflows in a non-English locale, ranked by how shipped products actually use them. (1) Shorten at translation time: Fresha's German CTAs stay 1-2 words by deliberate word choice ("Suchen", "Mehr erfahren", "Hol dir die App"), Treatwell compresses "Buche 24/7" the same way Solen's own copy-economy rule 1 already prescribes. (2) Widen the container to content: Booksy's German nav chip "Augenbrauen & Wimpern" (21 characters) ships unclamped at full pill width rather than truncated, alongside "Haarentfernung" (14 chars) and "Massage und Spa". (3) Wrap to a second line: Discord's language-settings row grows vertically to a second line for longer identifiers rather than truncating the first; Doctolib's German footer/legal nav reflows across multiple lines rather than clipping (partial evidence, footer-only fetch). None of the eight real apps sampled (N26, GetYourGuide, Discord, Trip.com, Fresha, Treatwell, Booksy, Doctolib) were observed using shrink-to-fit font scaling or mid-word ellipsis-truncation on a primary CTA or nav chip. This is usable negative evidence for D9: a hard-truncated DE/FR/IT CTA or chip in Solen's own audit is the anti-pattern these products avoid, not an acceptable fallback.

MECHANIC / MYTH-CHAIN FINDING (documented so it is not re-imported): a 2026 localization-trends article (gleef.eu, author credited only as "eva-b") states German expands "up to +30%" and cites a single source for it; fetching that cited source directly shows it is an SEO content-farm page (affiliate banners, unrelated "related reading" links, author credited as a "Retail Strategy Consultant") that does not contain the German percentage it is cited for. The same article states French +15-20%, Spanish +15-25%, and Arabic +20-30% with zero citations at all. This is the exact unsourced-stat-laundering shape SOURCE.md:1075's flat "German ~30%" already matched; it is now independently confirmed as folklore, not merely uncited.

SOURCE: W3C Internationalization Working Group, "Text size in translation" (Richard Ishida), https://www.w3.org/International/articles/article-text-size.en.html, citing IBM's "Guidelines to design global solutions" for the character-bucket table and its own Flickr "views" example for the per-language ratio. Competitor evidence: live fetches of fresha.com/de, treatwell.de, booksy.com/de-de, doctolib.de on 2026-07-22 (Doctolib partial, footer-only). Myth-chain evidence: gleef.eu "Top design localization trends every product team needs in 2026" and its cited unicode.live source, both fetched directly.

Companion edit to SOURCE.md:1075 (flag for owner sign-off, SOURCE.md sits above RATIONALE in doc hierarchy): change "German text expands ~30% vs English" to point at RATIONALE.md section 9 for the sourced mechanic, add FR/IT to the illustrative example line, and note the debunked gleef.eu citation chain so a future pass does not re-import the same folklore number from a trend search.
synth.generative_prior: Default fixed-width UI slots (chips, tabs, badge pills, button labels) to the length-dependent slack budget, not a flat percentage: under 10 EN characters, plan for 100-200% increase (2-3x length); 11-20 chars, 80-100%; 21-30 chars, 60-80%; 31-50 chars, 40-60%; over 70 chars, 30%. Do not use German as the single worst-case test string; include an Italian and French candidate too (Flickr "views": IT 3.0x > DE 2.8x > FR/PT 2.6x, T2). When a real DE/FR/IT string still overflows a slot sized to this budget, resolve it in this order, each demonstrated by a real shipped app: (1) shorten the copy itself, the way Fresha keeps CTAs to "Suchen" / "Mehr erfahren" and Treatwell to "Buche 24/7"; (2) let the container size to content, the way Booksy ships its 21-character "Augenbrauen & Wimpern" nav chip unclamped; (3) wrap to a second line, the way Discord's language row and Doctolib's footer nav reflow rather than truncate. Never shrink-to-fit or mid-word-ellipsis a CTA or nav chip; none of the eight real apps sampled do this.

synth.taste_lab_probe: Pull 12 real Solen strings across the four expansion bands (3 chips/badges under 10 EN chars, 3 tab/button labels 11-20 chars, 3 section titles/labels 21-30 chars, 3 body-adjacent labels 31-50+ chars) from the actual de/fr/it message-file values in messages/{locale}.json. For each, compute the real character-length ratio against the EN source and bucket it against the corrected MECHANIC table. Flag any string whose actual ratio exceeds its bucket's upper bound as a real overflow risk. Then, for every flagged string, check which of the three resolution strategies the component actually uses today: does it truncate/ellipsis (the anti-pattern, matches none of the 8 real apps sampled), does it clamp to a fixed width sized only against the EN or DE string (Booksy's counter-example says widen instead), or does it already wrap/size-to-content. This gives D9's overflow audit a numeric threshold AND a named pass/fail vocabulary (shorten / widen / wrap vs truncate) instead of the flat 30% folklore.

myths_caught: The draft's OWN myth-chain finding checked out as accurate (gleef.eu 'German +30%' traces to a unicode.live content-farm page by 'Lina Ortega, Retail Strategy Consultant' that does not contain the figure) - this is not a myth that snuck into the draft, it is a correctly-caught myth, verified independently via direct WebFetch of both pages.

Caught during this pass: the Treatwell 'Buche 24/7' example is presented as 'the primary CTA' compressed, but the live page shows it is a feature-section subheading ('Buche 24/7 / Einfach vom Bett oder aus dem Bus'), not the button text on Treatwell's actual primary CTA. The underlying fact (short, word-dropped German phrasing) is real; the framing overstated its UI role.

Caught during this pass: the Discord 'language-settings row grows to a second line for longer identifiers' claim overstates what Mobbin's Discord language-list screens actually show. Every row in that list is a static two-line design (native name + English name), used uniformly regardless of string length - not a dynamic wrap-on-overflow behavior. It is weak/wrong evidence for the specific 'wrap over truncate when a string overflows' mechanic, though it is still consistent with 'no truncation observed.'
verified.residual_risks: Owner-decision items: (1) SOURCE.md:1075 companion edit is correctly flagged in the draft itself as needing owner sign-off since SOURCE.md sits above RATIONALE in doc hierarchy - do not auto-apply. (2) The 51-70-char bucket genuinely does not monotonically decrease in IBM's own table (151-170% of original, i.e. 51-70% increase, sits above the 31-50 bucket's 40-60% increase) - this is a real property of the source data, not a synthesis error, but any implementer skimming the table for the first time will likely assume a typo; worth a one-line callout in RATIONALE itself, not just this verify pass. (3) Discord and N26 evidence came from Mobbin stock captures, not live-fetched originals like the four competitor sites - Discord's specific evidence for 'wrap on overflow' turned out to not support that exact mechanic (see myths_caught) and was cut; N26's 'natural-width row, no truncation' claim held up on re-check. Recommend the taste_lab_probe step lean on Booksy (verified, live, unclamped 21-char chip) and Doctolib (verified, live, wrapping footer) as the two strongest 'don't truncate' precedents rather than Discord. (4) The 'compounding languages is T1' tier claim (pre-existing content in RATIONALE.md, not net-new from this draft) is inflated - its only cited source is the same W3C secondary article, so T2 is the honest tier; flagging for a future pass since S33 does not touch that paragraph. (5) No search-engine cross-check of the exact D9-implementation numbers was possible beyond WebFetch (WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task by prior session usage) - all verification here is single-source WebFetch per claim, not multi-engine corroborated; low risk given every fetch returned exact-quote matches, but noted for completeness.
